mainTopic: Why רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר read the פסוק of 'בלא ראות' in opposite ways for a סומא in גלות, and a new משנה about a father who made a נדר against his son-in-law but still wants to give money to his daughter
overview: The amud opens with רבא answering an earlier difficulty about a סומא (blind person) who kills by accident. Each תנא seemed inconsistent about him. רבא explains that each one reads 'בלא ראות' (without seeing) in light of a different nearby word in the פסוקים. For רבי יהודה, 'forest' already includes a blind person, so 'בלא ראות' must exclude him from גלות. For רבי מאיר, 'without knowledge' already excludes him, so 'בלא ראות' must include him. Then a new משנה teaches that a father who forbade his son-in-law by נדר from benefiting from him can still give his daughter money. He gives it on condition that her husband has no rights to it, only for what she eats. In the גמרא, רב says only that exact wording works, while שמואל says even 'do whatever you want' keeps the money from the husband. רבי זירא then starts an objection, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבא: each תנא reads the verse from its context
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers the apparent contradiction by saying each תנא learns his view from the surrounding words of the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Here the ruling comes from the context of the verse, and there too it comes from the context of the verse.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a short, general answer to the earlier contradiction about a סומא. He is setting up the detailed explanations that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each תנא seemed to hold one view about a blind person in one place and the opposite view elsewhere. רבא says the difference is not a change of principle. Each one is reading the words 'בלא ראות' (without seeing) based on what the nearby words of the פסוק already teach.

keyTerms.meaning: from the context (subject matter) of the verse

phrases.english: Rava said:
Here it is from the context of the verse,
phrases.notes: He means each תנא gets his ruling by looking at the words around 'without seeing.'

phrases.english: and here it is from the context of the verse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a contradiction raised earlier about each תנא's view of a סומא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each opinion comes from a different reading of the context of the verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each תנא seems inconsistent about whether a סומא is included.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each one's reading of 'בלא ראות' comes from the context of the verse.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: 'forest' already includes the blind, so 'without seeing' excludes him
steps.stepSummary: For רבי יהודה, the word 'forest' already includes a סומא, so 'בלא ראות' must come to exclude him from גלות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה holds: about a killer it is written, 'One who goes into the forest with his fellow.' That includes anyone able to enter a forest, and a blind person can enter a forest. So if 'without seeing' came to include the blind, that is already known from 'forest.' Rather, 'without seeing' comes to exclude the blind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי יהודה reads the פסוקים about an accidental killer (רוצח בשוגג).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase about the forest covers anyone who can walk into a forest, and a blind person can. So there is no need for 'בלא ראות' to include him. Since the תורה does not waste words, 'בלא ראות' must teach the opposite: a סומא does not go to גלות.

keyTerms.meaning: a killer (here, one who killed by accident)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda holds:
Regarding a killer it is written:
"And one who comes with his fellow into the forest" —
this means anyone who is able to enter a forest,

phrases.aramaic: וְסּוֹמֵא נָמֵי בַּר מֵיעַל לְיַעַר הוּא.
phrases.english: and a blind person is also able to enter a forest.
And if you say
that "without seeing" comes to include the blind person —
he already learns that from "forest."
Rather, learn from it:
"without seeing" comes to exclude a blind person.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי יהודה סבר גבי רוצח כתיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out רבא's general answer for רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra wording must teach something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'בלא ראות' might come to include a blind person.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since 'forest' already includes him, 'בלא ראות' excludes a סומא from גלות.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: 'without knowledge' already excludes the blind, so 'without seeing' includes him
steps.stepSummary: For רבי מאיר, 'בבלי דעת' already excludes a סומא, so 'בלא ראות' must come to include him in גלות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר holds: it is written 'without knowledge.' That applies to anyone capable of knowing, and a blind person is not capable of knowing. So if 'without seeing' came to exclude the blind, that is already known from 'without knowledge.' Rather, 'without seeing' comes to include the blind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the opposite reading for רבי מאיר, using a different word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר focuses on 'בבלי דעת' (without knowledge). That phrase speaks about someone who could have known, and a blind person cannot. So the exclusion is already covered, and 'בלא ראות' must teach the reverse: a סומא does go to גלות. The same 'no wasted words' logic leads to opposite results because each תנא starts from a different word.
steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים use the same logic: 'בלא ראות' cannot repeat what another word already teaches. רבי יהודה starts from 'forest' (which includes the blind), so 'בלא ראות' excludes him. רבי מאיר starts from 'without knowledge' (which excludes the blind), so 'בלא ראות' includes him.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two: for רבי יהודה a סומא does NOT go to גלות; for רבי מאיר he DOES.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir holds:
It is written: "without knowledge" —
this means anyone who is capable of knowing,
and a blind person is not capable of knowing.
And if you say
that "without seeing" comes to exclude a blind person —
he already learns that from "without knowledge."
Rather, learn from it:
"without seeing" comes to include the blind person.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי מאיר סבר כתיב בבלי דעת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 2, giving רבי מאיר's reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra wording must teach something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'בלא ראות' might come to exclude a blind person.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since 'בבלי דעת' already excludes him, 'בלא ראות' includes a סומא in גלות.

steps.title: משנה: giving money to a daughter whose husband is forbidden by vow
steps.stepSummary: A father who forbade his son-in-law from benefiting from him can give his daughter money if he says it is only for what she eats, and her husband has no rights to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone vows that his son-in-law may not benefit from him, and he wants to give his daughter money, he says to her: 'This money is given to you as a gift, on condition that your husband has no rights to it, only to what you lift and put in your mouth.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches a way for a father to help his daughter even though his נדר forbids her husband from benefiting from him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally what a wife acquires goes to her husband, so a gift to her would benefit the son-in-law and break the נדר. The father avoids this by making a gift on condition that the husband has no rights in it, limited to her own food.

keyTerms.meaning: one who makes a vow forbidding benefit
what you lift and put in your mouth (your own food)

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who vows to forbid his son-in-law from benefiting from him,
and he wants to give his daughter money,
he says to her:
Behold, this money
is given to you as a gift,

phrases.aramaic: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא לְבַעְלִיךְ רְשׁוּת בָּהֶן,
phrases.english: provided that your husband will have no rights in it,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מָה שֶׁאַתְּ נוֹשֵׂאת וְנוֹתֶנֶת בְּפִיךְ.
phrases.english: only for what you lift up and put into your mouth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: a new משנה begins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father can give money to his daughter despite a נדר against her husband by giving it with the condition that the husband has no rights, only for her food.

steps.title: רב: only the exact wording of the משנה works
steps.stepSummary: רב says the משנה works only if the father limits it to her food; if he says 'do whatever you want,' the husband acquires it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: They taught this only where he said to her 'what you lift and put in your mouth.' But if he said 'do whatever you want with it,' the husband acquires the money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins, and רב limits the משנה to its exact wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, the condition 'your husband has no rights' only works when the gift is limited to her eating. If she is free to do anything with it, it is a normal gift to a wife, and the husband acquires it, which would break the נדר.

keyTerms.meaning: they taught this only (in a certain case)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rav said:
They taught this only

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר לַהּ ״מָה שֶׁאַתְּ נוֹשֵׂאת וְנוֹתֶנֶת בְּפִיךְ״,
phrases.english: where he said to her, "what you lift up and put into your mouth,"
but if he said, "do with it whatever you want,"
the husband acquires them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the משנה's ruling to its exact wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only 'what you put in your mouth' works; 'do whatever you want' lets the husband acquire the money.

steps.title: שמואל: even 'do whatever you want' works
steps.stepSummary: שמואל disagrees with רב: even with 'do whatever you want,' the husband does not acquire the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל says: Even if he said 'do whatever you want,' the husband does not acquire the money.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the opposite view to רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, the condition that the husband has no rights works even when the daughter may use the money freely. The משנה's wording 'what you put in your mouth' is just one example, not a requirement.

phrases.english: And Shmuel says:
Even if he said, "do whatever you want" —
the husband does not acquire them.

steps.triggerLanguage: ושמואל אומר אפילו אמר מה שתרצי עשי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב's narrowing of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even with 'do whatever you want,' the husband does not acquire the money.

steps.title: רבי זירא begins an objection
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא starts to challenge the previous statement; the details of his objection come next.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. רבי זירא is about to challenge רב's statement, and the actual question comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מתקיף לה' signals a strong objection is coming. The content of the challenge continues on the next amud. Here we only know that an attack on the previous ruling is starting.

keyTerms.meaning: he objected to it (raised a strong challenge)

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira objected to it:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge to the statement just made.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's statement about the wording of the gift
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Not stated on this amud; the objection continues on the next amud.
